correctness.rationale: Complete rank-two FO signatures are sets of pointed rank-one witness patterns. This is proved in both directions by normal forms and rank-two defining sentences. Every structure reduces without changing that invariant by capping each red and blue class population at 2 and each resulting class type multiplicity at 2. There are exactly 3^8-1=6560 nonempty profiles. All are exhaustively checked with two independent exact logical invariants; the resulting quotient has 207 types, minimum-representative size distribution 2,6,10,17,22,28,30,29,26,18,12,5,2 over sizes 1 through 13, and two explicitly listed 13-element sharp representatives. No finite data are extrapolated beyond the proved cap reduction. Source: RESULT.md theorem/proof; direct verifier verify_rank2.py and its exact assertions.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact 207 complete rank-two theories, sharp 13-element minimum, two extremal types, eight coloured block patterns and the full histogram against the indexed published mathematical statements and the most directly relevant 2015 primary full text. Pratt-Hartmann addresses decision problems for richer two-variable logic with counting, not the exact numbers derived here. Prior uncoloured equivalence classifications cannot imply the colour-block mixing distinction without additional theory. Narrow finite priority remains subject to possible unindexed tables; no stronger covering claim was encountered.

value.rationale: A complete and sharp finite-model rank-two profile for the canonical structures formed by equivalence classes with arbitrary unary colouring is a motivated natural classification. It simultaneously resolves all 207 complete theories, the sharp 13-vertex smallest-model upper bound, the two unique worst-case theory types and the full size distribution. Class colour mixing creates an invariant genuinely absent from the uncoloured equivalence setting; a reusable pointed-signature reduction accounts for all structures before computing the exact finite counts. The work does not depend for its value on an unsupported downstream theorem.
